svg.title: The British Sector of the Western Front: Terrain, Key Battles & Medical Context (1914–1918)
svg.desc: True 1:10m GIS atlas map of Flanders, Artois, Picardy, the Strait of Dover, and South-East England (1914–18), illustrating the stabilised Western Front from Nieuwpoort through the Ypres Salient and Passchendaele, Loos, Vimy Ridge, Arras (Thompson’s Cave underground hospital), the Somme (57,470 Day-1 casualties), and the 1917 Hindenburg Line at Cambrai (476 tanks and Capt. Oswald Robertson’s stored blood bank), alongside coastal Base Hospitals at Calais, Boulogne, and Étaples and the Dover/Folkestone hospital-ship lifeline.

g.text: Nieuwpoort → Ypres Salient → Loos → Arras → Somme

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 1 (SECTION A): THE BRITISH SECTOR OF THE WESTERN FRONT, 1914–18 (KT5.1)
The British Sector of the Western Front: Terrain, Key Battles & Medical Context (1914–18)
Terrain directly shaped wounds and evacuation: waterlogged Flanders clay at Ypres caused trench foot and gas gangrene, chalk at Arras
enabled 700-bed underground Thompson’s Cave, Somme (57,470 Day-1 casualties) strained triage, and Cambrai (1917) pioneered stored blood.
